answer: What I'd try is letting graders quietly swap their vote using a fresh key right up until the panel closes, with only the last one counting. Nobody, including whoever paid them, can tell which vote was final. So if someone rents fifty aged accounts to wave through an opal import appraisal or a basalt core sample report, they can't check they got what they paid for, since any seller can flip it after cashing in. The kernel of this comes from MACI-style voting. It makes renting or buying accounts close to worthless, so the attacker has to build and run every clone himself.
